channel.title: Weekly Worker — Imperialism & War (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker — Imperialism & War.

item.title: Deterrents real and imagined
item.description: The present stand-off in the Gulf could run and run. Or there could be a sudden escalation. It is impossible to say, argues Yassamine Mather. Meanwhile, the situation inside Iran grows ever more desperate for working people
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Two takes on a genocidal nightmare
item.description: Anne McShane reviews Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (directors) NAZA. Daniele Rugo and Kyle Oakeson (directors) Life support. Both on general release
item.dc:creator: Anne McShane

item.title: Low expectations
item.description: Reportedly, it was the economy that sank Trump and the Republicans in the midterms … that and the unpopular Iran war. Yet, even with a clear majority in both houses, the Democrats are not going to bring about major change. And then there is the AI bubble, says Michael Roberts
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: A hidden supreme leader
item.description: Irrationalist belief in divination, spirit contact, haloes and jinn armies grows above. Below, living standards are falling and protests are reviving. Yassamine Mather looks at the two worlds that make up the Islamic Republic
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: No clear outcome
item.description: There will be weeks of haggling, offers of bribes and ominous threats of all kinds. The Arab-majority parties might well be involved in this grubby business. But when it comes to the oppression of the Palestinians within and without Israel, no fundamental change should be expected, argues Yassamine Mather
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Modern wars, ancient myths
item.description: As the flame of war spreads across the region, Yassamine Mather looks at Saudi Arabia’s vulnerability, the misinformation surrounding the Houthis and Marco Rubio’s dangerous clash of civilisations nonsense
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Prisoners in soft captivity
item.description: Does British promotion of European rearmament against Russia amount to a viable alternative to US domination? Mike Macnair does not think so. Europe is incapable of independent action
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: The last man of ideas
item.description: Paul Demarty reviews Francis Fukuyama In the realm of the last man London 2026, pp304, £20
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Three years of genocide
item.description: Millions marched worldwide, in London over 200,000. No one is fooled by Ed Miliband’s weasel words, not least because of the continued arms trade with Israel and the ban on Palestine Action, says Ian Spencer
item.dc:creator: Ian Spencer

item.title: Realities of siege warfare
item.description: Internationalists oppose US imperialism and simultaneously maintain complete political independence from the Islamic Republic. The struggles of the working class and the poor are central, declares Yassamine Mather
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Three years of genocidal war
item.description: Zack Polanski’s Green Party is being demonised as racist because it opposes Zionist racism and dares call for a single-state solution. But is the single state, as traditionally demanded by Palestinian militants and the revolutionary left, actually achievable? What about the two-state solution? Jack Conrad presents the communist view
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Hacking in a fragile world
item.description: As the FBI has found to its cost, from state actors to trivial script-kiddies, hackers are on the attack. The networked world is more vulnerable than ever. But why? asks Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Notes on space
item.description: US airforce secretary Troy Meink has confirmed what we long knew: America has deployed ‘space control weapons’ in low Earth orbit. While details remain unclear, the dangers are all too evident. Jack Conrad argues that space display, space science and space war have a symbiotic relationship
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Threats, walkouts and secret talks
item.description: Trump set the tone. From the podium of an organisation supposedly founded to prevent war between states, he mused about the “annihilation” of Iran. Yassamine Mather looks at the theatre that is the UN general assembly
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Vote for Palestine
item.description: Elections always involve difficult tactical calculations. We favour voting and active participation over sitting on the sidelines in the name of purity. Zack Polanski has supported the pro-Palestine protests and now calls himself an ‘anti-Zionist’. On October 8 that should count. Carla Roberts weighs the pros and cons
item.dc:creator: Carla Roberts

item.title: How did we get here?
item.description: To understand the wars engulfing the Middle East today, it is not enough to begin with the February 28 combined assault on Iran by the US and Israel or even October 7 2023 and Gaza, says Yassamine Mather
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: A demand of enduring relevance
item.description: With the world seemingly headed towards another generalised war, Marcus Strom argues that a popular militia and democratic self-defence is the best option for workers in Australia. Not Aukus and nuclear-powered subs
item.dc:creator: Marcus Strom

item.title: Before and after 9/11
item.description: Three times as many people have died from the toxic pollution caused by the September 11 2001 attack on the Twin Towers than the attack itself - but other questions remain. Carla Roberts and Alex Maxwell look back 25 years
item.dc:creator: Alex Maxwell
Carla Roberts

item.title: Demand the whole package
item.description: Ed Miliband has given an inch. Even though it is a token, we should be encouraged and take renewed strength. Yassamine Mather calls for full sanctions, boycotts and strikes
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Notes on the war
item.description: Trump’s second peace plan has had the same success as his first. Jack Conrad warns that not only is the war set to continue, things will probably get ever more painful. But what about the possibility of revolution?
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Palestine picket line
item.description: There are more and more government sanctions from above and economic, cultural and sporting boycotts from below. Carl Collins shows that this phenomenon has a long and highly contested history
item.dc:creator: Carl Collins

item.title: Rise of the robots
item.description: Headlines have been about outrunning Usain Bolt, playing football and learning to kickbox in just a couple of hours. But, explains Yassamine Mather, the development of humanoid and other such robots is about far more than entertainment and mere spectacle
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather
